- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or erratic, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to compensate for downward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 5–10% from forecast for 2–3 periods.
- If model forecast is >15% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast toward historical mean (last 10–15 days) by 1–3% per period.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “sentiment pivot” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% starting from the period of sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), model often misses it — adjust downward by 3–8% in first 3 periods.
